summary: Create a board capability. The board’s filtering, authorization-aware label attachment, grouping, and cross-capability coordination are meaningful application policy; placing them in the page would make the route a business layer, while placing them in work-items would couple two independently changeable capabilities. The RSC page remains a thin channel boundary.

tree.purpose: RSC entry point. Establishes request identity, invokes the board RSC surface, and renders route-private loading/error/empty/board presentation.
Server-only public surface for the board page. Accepts trusted request identity and exposes getBoard().

Owns orchestration and board policy: fetch visible work items, remove archived items, obtain referenced visible labels, reject forbidden label references, attach label details, and group items by status.
Board-owned capability-shaped ports such as WorkItemReader and LabelReader; their methods return only the fields required by board policy.
Pure BoardView, BoardColumn, BoardItem, and BoardLabel types plus deterministic grouping/projection rules where useful.
Private adapters implementing board ports by calling work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts public trusted APIs; wires reporter and request context.
Existing narrow trusted-server surface used by board; exposes an actor-scoped read returning validated work-item values, never persistence rows.
Existing narrow trusted-server surface used by board; resolves requested label IDs under actor/tenant visibility rules and distinguishes forbidden or missing references.
Capability-private persistence adapter enforcing tenant/ownership predicates or RLS.
Capability-private persistence adapter enforcing tenant/visibility predicates or RLS.
Unit tests board outcomes with fake ports: archive filtering, grouping, label joining, forbidden-label rejection, missing labels, duplicates, and deterministic ordering.
Tests authentication propagation, expected failure mapping, unexpected exception reporting exactly once, and redaction.
RSC integration tests rendered success, empty, denied, and failure states using public boundaries.
Asserts board alone imports both public server surfaces, work-items and labels never import each other, internals are not imported cross-module, and client code cannot import server surfaces.

flows: Request → src/app/board/page.tsx → authenticate once and construct actor/tenant/role/request/trace identity → src/modules/board/rsc.ts → getBoard().
getBoard() → WorkItemReader.listVisible(identity) → work-items/server.ts → work-items store/RLS. The operation then removes archived items and collects referenced label IDs.
getBoard() → LabelReader.resolveVisible(identity, referencedIds) → labels/server.ts → labels store/RLS. This call is sequential because its IDs come from the filtered work items.

getBoard() verifies every referenced label has an allowed resolution; any forbidden reference rejects the board result rather than silently leaking or partially attaching it. It then attaches safe label projections, groups by status, and returns BoardView to the RSC page.

Expected outcomes such as board access denied or forbidden label references return typed application results. The RSC boundary maps them to the chosen route behavior, such as notFound, access-denied UI, or a safe error state. Unexpected database defects/outages throw, are reported once at rsc.ts with request/trace context and redacted metadata, then reach the route error boundary. Framework control-flow exceptions remain outside generic catches.

decisions.rationale: The deletion test shows real board-owned policy and coordination. Neither source capability naturally owns the combined projection.

decisions.choice: app → board → work-items and labels public server surfaces
decisions.rationale: This keeps the graph acyclic and prevents work-items and labels from importing or changing with each other.

decisions.choice: Only board/rsc.ts externally; work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts for trusted adapters
decisions.rationale: The page needs one board-shaped operation, while cross-capability reads remain narrow, server-only, and persistence-agnostic.

decisions.choice: Authenticate at the RSC/server boundary; enforce board access and forbidden-label policy in board application code; enforce tenant/ownership/visibility again in each owning store or RLS
decisions.rationale: Each layer protects the concern it owns without trusting caller-supplied scope.

decisions.choice: Fetch work items first, then labels by referenced IDs
decisions.rationale: Label inputs depend on the filtered work-item result, so parallel fetching would either over-fetch or weaken authorization intent.

decisions.choice: Rendering and channel-native error behavior only
decisions.rationale: Business filtering, joining, and grouping must remain testable and discoverable under the owning capability.

risks: If existing trusted APIs cannot distinguish forbidden labels from missing labels, labels/server.ts needs a safe typed resolution contract; collapsing both states could prevent the board from enforcing its rejection policy correctly.
Returning unrestricted labels or raw provider rows would widen data exposure; both source surfaces must project and validate capability-owned values.
Silent omission of forbidden labels can disclose relationship information or render a misleading partial board; rejection semantics must be explicit.

Cache ownership remains with work-items and labels. Any future mutations should invalidate their capability tags; a board aggregate tag should be added only if the board surface actually caches the combined projection.
A broad catch in the page and another in board/rsc.ts could double-report failures; designate board/rsc.ts as the single reporting boundary.
